title: So many people are wasting resources.
author: KitKatBarMan
selftext:
Honestly, I think a lot of people are pouring a surprising amount of time, money, compute, and energy into using AI to turn half-baked ideas into technically finished products that almost nobody is ever going to use. There are thousands of little games, apps, and experiments being generated that might get shown to a few friends, posted online once, and then forgotten. Individually that isn't a big deal, but when you multiply it across millions of people, it starts to feel like a pretty substantial use of resources for very little lasting value.

The part that bothers me isn't that people are making games or doing creative things. People should absolutely be able to make things for fun. It's the opportunity cost. These same tools are becoming capable enough to help with scientific research, medicine, engineering, education, accessibility, infrastructure, and thousands of boring but genuinely useful problems that historically haven't gotten enough attention because they were too difficult or expensive to work on. If we're suddenly giving ordinary people access to this much computational leverage, it seems worth asking whether we should be pointing more of it toward problems that actually improve people's lives.

Obviously not every AI project needs to cure cancer or save the world. Hobbies and entertainment have value too. But I do think there's something strange about having one of the most powerful new technologies we've developed in decades and using an enormous amount of its capacity to mass-produce disposable games, clones, and novelty apps. Even redirecting a small fraction of that effort toward useful research, open-source tools, local problems, or neglected scientific questions could probably create a lot more value for society.

comments.author: GigaTerra
comments.body:
This comment you made, used more resources than most AI do when operating.

Don't get me wrong, CEOs are wasting resources in training, that is not necessary. But your post is about what users use. The simple fact is Social media, like Reddit post, are using way more resources. All AI in 2026 is using less than 1% (0.1%) compared to all social media. However even this is an tiny fraction of resources used by humans. For example all of social media uses \~1% of the electricity needed to produce an car.

In other words humans can make 1 car, an 100 social media posts, or ask an AI 1000 questions.

You see why Pro-AI people are annoyed with the Anti-AI post, it is like complaining about the salt someone puts on chips, while you enjoy an dry-brine stake.

replies.author: KitKatBarMan
replies.body: What are you talking about? The models have a sunk cost of training that gets spread out over the lifetime of usage. So even if a users question doesn't cost much, the models training and resource use is still there.

replies.author: GigaTerra
replies.body:
But you are talking about what users are using. The training cost is there if 1 person uses AI, or every single human does. 

CEOs where spending those resources even before AI was popular, because it is not based on user income, it is based on investor income. So even if no one used AI, the training would go on all the same, till the money is dry. That is why spending was so bad, even before AI was popular.

Also don't forget, my summary above was just user side costs. If we factor in Data centers costs for social media, social media is still doing the most harm to the planet, and it is only in 2028-2030 that projections think AI will do more harm.

The two of us having this discussion, is doing great harm to the world right now.

comments.author: emperormarkus
comments.body:
I think this is missing the real value here of what people are doing with AI.

Sure there is some computing and data usage going on. I think it is a fraction of what is already being used by businesses.

The true value is engagement and creativity. People are getting into making games. It doesn’t matter their true quality. They are getting to use new technology to produce something that they are tailoring to what they want to play. That is really exciting.

Eventually this will disrupt traditional game makers. But I am not bothered about that. Disruption happens to all industries.

They are finding a way to use tools that they have to become proficient at in the workplace in their personal lives in a way that really benefits their hobbies and leisure time. That has to be a good thing.

I have learned so many new things in just months of using various AI tools. I make and post games that I like. I get some feedback and have had a good amount of downloads and games played. That’s fine. I don’t have to change the world with what I make.

It is an also a great medium to connect with my child. We make and play test games together. We are having a great time. For me this feels like real quality time.

Hope someone uses AI for all sorts of medical and health discoveries. Doesn’t have to be all of us.
